excerpt: Identify the providers and account arrangements for the exact address. Electricity, water, cooling and internet may follow separate steps, even when the keys are ready.
introduction:
A home can be available to enter before it is ready for an ordinary evening. The lights may work during a viewing while the new account remains unresolved. Internet may be available in the building but still require an appointment inside the unit. Cooling can involve a separate provider or billing arrangement.

Treat service setup as a small project with named providers and confirmation numbers. The process depends on the address, occupancy arrangement and emirate. The examples here explain why those differences matter; they are not one set of instructions that can be applied to every UAE home.
takeaways: Identify the provider and account holder for every essential service at the exact unit.
Distinguish an application, payment, appointment and confirmed working service.
Check actual connectivity and billing after moving, and retain the setup records.

sections.heading: Create an address-specific service list
sections.body:
Ask the landlord, developer or building manager which organisations serve the property and which services are included in the agreement. List electricity, water, cooling, gas where applicable, internet and any building-specific service that affects occupation. Record the unit and relevant premises identifiers carefully; a similar building name is not enough.

Clarify whose name each account should be in and what documents are required for your situation. Owners, tenants and occupants of serviced accommodation may follow different arrangements. If a service is included, find out what the inclusion covers and whom to contact if it fails.

Do not assume that one payment activates everything. Keep a separate status for each service and identify the earliest sensible application date. Confirm whether technicians need access, management permission or a particular person present. These details can affect the move even when the administrative application is straightforward.

sections.heading: Use the electricity and water process that applies to you
sections.body:
[DEWA's move-in service](https://dewa.gov.ae/en/about-us/service-guide/consumer-services/move-in) explains its integration with Ejari for relevant Dubai tenancies; owners and other specified cases use separate applications. Check the account notification, required payment and activation status for your circumstances. An existing supply at a viewing is not confirmation that your own account is ready.

In Abu Dhabi, [TAQA Distribution's move-in guide](https://www.addc.ae/en-US/residential/Pages/About-Moving-in.aspx) distinguishes tenancies linked through Tawtheeq or ADGM from owners and other cases needing an application. Use the provider's current instructions for the actual address. Do not assume a Dubai registration number belongs in an Abu Dhabi process.

For another emirate or a special arrangement, confirm the relevant provider directly. Avoid building your plan around a friend's historic fee or activation time. Retain the request reference and receipt, and follow up through the official channel if the expected confirmation does not arrive. A service target is not a reason to leave no practical margin before occupation.

sections.heading: Ask how cooling and other services are charged
sections.body:
Find out whether cooling is part of the electricity bill, separately metered, paid through a district-cooling account or included under the tenancy's terms. Ask for the applicable provider and current tariff explanation where relevant. A marketing phrase such as chiller-free needs to be understood in the actual agreement, including any exclusions.

Separate consumption charges from standing, capacity, administration or other applicable amounts. Request an explanation of the categories rather than estimating the next bill from the thermostat setting alone. Historic bills may help with questions, but they reflect another household's usage and conditions and do not guarantee your costs.

If the home uses gas or has equipment that needs commissioning, arrange the correct qualified provider and access process. Do not attempt connections or modifications yourself. Keep the household's move-in decision tied to services being safely ready, rather than simply to the delivery date.

sections.heading: Arrange internet for the exact unit and work pattern
sections.body:
Ask the provider what service is available at the specific unit, not merely in the neighbourhood. Compare the contract duration, installation, equipment, recurring price and any early-exit or relocation terms. Promotional pricing should be separated from the normal charge after the offer ends.

If transferring an existing eLife service, [e&'s Home Move guidance](https://www.eand.ae/en/c/home/home-moving.html) distinguishes the old home's disconnection date from installation at the new address. It also tells customers to take their router and related equipment while leaving the building's ONT device. Follow the instructions for your actual provider and setup rather than removing fixed equipment by assumption.

Explain where you need a reliable connection, particularly if several people work or study at once. A plan's advertised access speed and the Wi-Fi experience in a distant room are different questions. Confirm installation access and discuss the in-home arrangement with the provider before committing to a desk location that cannot be served conveniently.

sections.heading: Schedule a readiness check before the main delivery
sections.body:
Where access permits, visit before the removal van arrives and confirm the essential services with the responsible parties. Check the actual account status as well as what is visibly working. Keep a list of unresolved issues and the reference for each one so follow-up calls can be specific.

Arrange installation appointments with the building's access requirements in mind. A technician arriving while the lift is occupied by a removal crew may not be able to complete the planned work. The [moving-day checklist](/journal/uae-moving-day-checklist) helps coordinate those activities and keep the first-night essentials accessible.

Have a practical contingency if connectivity is not ready for an important work commitment. Discuss temporary arrangements with your employer or provider rather than assuming a mobile connection will support every task. The [home-working layout guide](/journal/working-from-home-uae-layout) explains why location within the home, noise and shared routines also matter.

sections.heading: Check the first bills and close the old arrangements
sections.body:
Review the first statements for the correct name, premises, billing period and agreed plan. Separate refundable deposits from usage and other charges. If an amount is unclear, ask the provider to explain it while the application and receipts are easy to retrieve. Keep the response with the account record.

When relocating from another home, confirm the old account's closure or transfer separately. Avoid assuming the new setup cancels every previous service. Check the provider's instructions about equipment, final charges and any refund, and do not disconnect services belonging to another lawful occupant.

Store account references securely and make sure the household knows how to report a fault without sharing passwords unnecessarily. Once the services are working and the records are correct, the setup project can close. The goal is a home that functions reliably, with a clear route for resolving problems if they arise.
